title: Training Notes: Maintenance Recency on Harbison Labor-Only Protection Claims
content:
These notes answer the questions new care centre agents raise about the maintenance-recency share on claims against the Harbison 5-Year Labor Protection and the Harbison 10-Year Labor Protection, the labor-only tiers of Harbison Protection Contracts.

**What is the maintenance-recency share, and what does it act on?**
It is a share applied by multiplication to the labor allowed on a labor-only claim. It is set by the latest documented maintenance completed on or before the failure date.

**Which records are read?**
Three records: the failed unit's most recent heating-season Comfort Club tune-up, its most recent cooling-season Comfort Club tune-up — both completed visits recorded under the holder's Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements — and the most recent precision tune-up charge line on the holder's Harbison invoices. Each of these three records counts only when it is dated on or before the failure date, because maintenance done after a failure is no evidence of care before it.

**How is the share fixed?**
The latest counting record is measured in whole calendar months to the failure date (the completed date of the claim's service call):

| Whole calendar months from the latest counting record to the failure date | Maintenance-recency share |
|---|---|
| 12 months or more, or no counting record at all | 0.85 |
| 9 to 11 months | 0.95 |
| fewer than 9 months | 1 |

**Where do the thresholds fall?** 8 months takes 1; 9 months takes 0.95; 11 months takes 0.95; 12 months takes 0.85.

**Can you show it with dates?** (hypothetical) Latest counting tune-up completed 2 February 2025:

- failure date 1 November 2025: 8 whole months — share 1;
- failure date 2 November 2025: 9 whole months — share 0.95;
- failure date 2 February 2026: 12 whole months — share 0.85.

**What if the most recent tune-up came after the failure?**
That record does not count. Hypothetically, a unit's most recent cooling-season tune-up is dated after the failure date and its most recent heating-season tune-up is dated before it: only the heating-season tune-up (and any precision tune-up line dated on or before the failure) is measured.

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** A labor allowed of $800.00 with the latest counting record 10 whole months before the failure: $800.00 multiplied by 0.95 is $760.00.
